assumptions: Native count remains 1..16; no bijection assumption on maps; caller-supplied handle validity is checked separately at each operation
Relational RAM shim admits aligned timer-region words only, normalizes segment access, and does not model concurrent instruction-level delivery
Proofs allow arbitrary interval high bits/zero, countdown underflow/overflow, due low bits and corrupted other mapping values; no unsigned-positive time invariant is imposed

Original code is single CPU with word writes atomic. Remove does PUSHF/CLI around updates; setter resolves handle BEFORE CLI, then updates under CLI; register publishes last slot only after initialization and masks interrupts only when lowering earliest

Original registration writes interval/countdown/pointer words before publishing last; this helps visibility but is not a proved general reentrancy protocol. Saved BIOS callback executes STI, allowing nesting. Native guarantees serialized calls and explicit between-callback mutation only

Successful named lifecycle supports [BIOS, playback, optional fade] with capacity <=3 and tail removals, because shutdown cancels fade before playback. This is a static conditional finding, not a proved global reachable-state exclusion

Failed init retains attempted flag and stale handle; open callback API and mid-instruction IRQ schedules are outside that successful-lifecycle argument. Defects are retained, so native correctness does not depend on excluding moved removal
